_comment: KPI gates — the pass/fail contract a deployment must satisfy before it is accepted.
This file is the SINGLE source of truth for what 'a working deployment' means. It is read
by tools/kpi-gate/kpi_gate.py (the gate) and by ci/scripts/collect-kpis.sh (the snapshot),
so a threshold can never drift between what CI enforces and what is reported.
Every 'expr' is written against metric names VERIFIED in docs/evidence/ — not guessed.
free5gc_amf_business_ue_cm_gmm_state_count. Measured against nr-cli ground truth at the
same instant they read 3 and 63 while 20/20 UEs were genuinely registered — wrong in
opposite directions. They leak on aborted procedures and never reset. A gate built on an
untrustworthy signal is worse than no gate, so UE population is taken from the slice
exporter, which derives it from AMF logs.

gates.title: All 8 control-plane NFs are scrapeable
gates.why: An NF that cannot be scraped is either down or has metrics disabled. Either way the deployment is not observable, which is the thing this project exists to guarantee.

gates.title: No configured target is down
gates.why: Catches the failure mode where the core is healthy but the observability plane itself has broken — a silently blind pipeline still reports green without this.

gates.title: Expected UE population is registered
gates.why: The deployment is only accepted if devices actually attached. Sourced from the slice exporter (AMF logs), not the AMF gauges, which are known to be wrong.

gates.title: Both slices have registered UEs
gates.why: 20 UEs all on one slice would pass a naive count while slicing is entirely broken. This is the check that would have caught the 'AMF can not select an target AMF by NRF' failure.

gates.title: Subscriber records exist for both slices
gates.why: Provisioning silently under-running is a real observed failure (duplicate GPSI aborts the loop part-way), and it looks identical to a RAN problem from the UE side.

gates.title: SBI server-error rate is below threshold
gates.why: Sustained 5xx between network functions means the core is misconfigured even when every container is up. PDU-session paths are excluded because they fail by design without a UPF (R-01).

gates.title: SBI p95 latency within budget
gates.why: Inter-NF latency is the earliest signal that the host is too loaded to serve the core honestly. Mirrors the SbiLatencyHigh alert so the gate and the alerting agree.

gates.title: Both slices publish capacity
gates.why: If the orchestrator cannot read the subscriber database it reports no capacity, and every later allocation number would be meaningless.

gates.title: No slice is saturated
gates.why: Advisory, not a gate: saturation under a deliberate load test is the correct behaviour, not a defect. It is reported so a regression in allocation policy is visible.

gates.title: No demand refused for want of a low-latency slice
gates.why: A latency refusal means no permitted slice could meet the requirement — a provisioning gap rather than a capacity one. Advisory because it is a property of the offered load.

gates.title: PDU session establishment succeeds
gates.why: The real user-plane KPI. Requires gtp5g and therefore the ODE; reported SKIP-ODE here rather than silently passing, because a gate that cannot run has not been met.

gates.title: Per-slice throughput matches the provisioned AMBR
gates.why: Closes the loop from modelled capacity to measured throughput. Impossible without a UPF, so it is declared here and skipped, keeping the gap explicit instead of forgotten.
